title: Oh, Maya!  I was lucky enough to watch Maya Rudolph make her Broadway...
transcript: Maya Rudolph in Oh Mary is one of those dream casts that you see online and think, well, that would be really cool, but it's never gonna happen. And yet, here we are. Maya Rudolph has made her Broadway debut in Oh Mary, and of course, I had to be there for her opening night. One of the interesting things about her Mary is she actually starts the show pretty subdued and then gets increasingly more manic as the show goes on. Now, more subdued Marys have worked in the past. I think Jane Krakowski is a great example of that. But in Maya's case, I definitely prefer the more manic side of her performance, when she really started to be able to ham it up. And gives you a lot of the things that you would expect with Maya Rudolph in this role. She's making faces, she's doing voices. I actually really loved anytime her character was reading Shakespeare, because you never knew what voice was going to come out of her mouth next. But the more I think about it, the more I actually do appreciate Maya's more subdued start, because it grounds the character in a way that I wasn't expecting from Maya Rudolph. It had me invested in the character in ways that I haven't necessarily been in the past. You're able to see the human being underneath the grandiose persona. And it's a really tough line to walk where you are capturing both the absurdity and also The sincerity. But Maya Rudolph is able to do both, and I think that's what really made her marry for me. Obviously, this was her first performance, and I'm really excited to see how she grows with the role as she gets more comfortable with it. But even just based on what I saw tonight, I do think that audiences that get a chance to see her are in for a treat.
